canonical_statement: The investigators performed an audit of heparin treatment to assess therapeutic control and clinicians' responses to out-of-range kaolin cephalin clotting times.
For the audit, the therapeutic kaolin cephalin clotting time range was defined as 1.5 to 2.5 times the control value.

canonical_statement: The investigators analysed clinicians' responses to kaolin cephalin clotting times outside the therapeutic range by examining subsequent changes in heparin infusion rate.

For 28 patients, the investigators constructed dose-response curves and calculated the heparin infusion rate required to produce a kaolin cephalin clotting time of 60 seconds, corresponding to 1.5 times the local control value.
Across 180 heparin days, the kaolin cephalin clotting time was within the therapeutic range on 45 days.

canonical_statement: The study found no significant relation between the therapeutic heparin infusion rate and patient age or weight.

The authors concluded that heparin control in their hospital was poor, citing ignored KCT results, adjustments made in the wrong direction, and frequent failure of remaining adjustments to achieve the therapeutic range.
The authors concluded that the lack of a significant control difference between infusion pumps and nurse-operated burettes implied that factors other than infusion device affected heparin control.
The authors recommended smaller increments in heparin infusion rate as the kaolin cephalin clotting time approaches the therapeutic range.
The authors stated that individual titration of the heparin infusion rate is necessary to optimize efficiency and reduce potential toxicity.
The authors advised that both prolonged and shortened kaolin cephalin clotting times should not be ignored during heparin treatment.
